brief.subject: Diesel jumps 9.7 cents; $12M cargo theft case; trailer orders soar
brief.headline: Diesel Climbs 9.7 Cents to $6.276 as Cargo Theft and Equipment Buying Heat Up
brief.dek: Diesel rose for the week, feds charged a driver in a $12M identity-theft scheme, and trailer orders spiked 385% in September.
brief.lede: The national diesel average rose 9.7 cents to $6.276 per gallon, a fresh hit to per-mile costs even after a four-week decline.

sections.heading: Diesel Turns Higher Again
bullets: $6.276 per gallon is the U.S. average retail diesel price for the week of 2026-10-19.
Up 9.7 cents (1.6%) from the prior week, squeezing margins on loads booked without a fuel surcharge.
Down 25.3 cents over four weeks, so the weekly jump erases part of the recent relief.
Check that fuel surcharge tables on current contracts reflect this week's price before quoting new lanes.

sections.heading: $12M Theft Ring Used Hijacked Carrier IDs
bullets: At least 24 shipments disappeared after drivers picked up freight at distribution centers, federal authorities say.
Investigators found fake licenses, altered identities and ransom demands tied to the scheme.
Hijacked authorities can damage a real carrier's reputation, so monitor your credentials and broker setup records closely.

sections.heading: Trailer Orders Jump Ahead of Price Hikes
bullets: 385% surge in U.S. trailer orders in September as carriers locked in equipment before possible price increases.
Class 8 truck purchases sent mixed signals, showing fleets are cautious about power units.
EPA '27 NOx engine rules are approaching and will affect anyone buying new heavy-duty trucks.

sections.heading: Railroads Post Record Quarters
bullets: Union Pacific reported record Q3 revenue and profits as volume and pricing gains outpaced fuel and inflation costs.
Norfolk Southern also hit record Q3 revenue on higher volumes, rates and fuel surcharges.
Strong rail pricing and volume suggest intermodal remains a competitor on long-haul lanes.

sections.heading: Port Dwell Times Climb at San Pedro Bay
bullets: Record September volumes at San Pedro Bay ports pushed up cargo dwell times for both rail and truck.
Longer dwell means more waiting at terminals, so drayage carriers should factor detention into rates.
